headline: Every bottle of prosecco checked, not a sample.
label: #F7F2E6
heroLede: Prosecco, pinot grigio and Italian reds look much the same in the bottle, so the label is what tells them apart. Here's what a camera check could look like on your bottling line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every bottle has its closure on, straight and fully seated. A crooked closure on sparkling wine means lost pressure and a flat bottle.
labelLede: Prosecco and pinot grigio can share a bottle shape and look much the same at speed. The camera checks every bottle carries the right label for the wine inside, straight and intact.
codeLede: The lot code ties every bottle back to its tank and vintage. The system reads the printed code on every bottle and compares it with the wine and lot set at changeover.
objectLede: Glass fragments, capsule offcuts and loose parts can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four crooked closures in fifteen minutes. Check the closer.
